title: Sizing and box-sizing
summary: Set width, max-width and height, and use box-sizing so padding does not break your sizes.

quiz.q: With the default `box-sizing: content-box`, how wide in px is the box on screen, counting padding and border?
quiz.explain: The width applies to the content only: 200 + 20 + 20 for padding + 5 + 5 for border = 250px.

quiz.q: Now add `box-sizing: border-box`. How wide is the box on screen in px?
quiz.explain: With `border-box`, the width includes padding and border. The content shrinks to fit. This is much easier to plan with.

quiz.q: Why is `max-width: 100%` useful on an image?
options: It makes the image always 100% wide
It stops the image from growing wider than its container
quiz.explain: `max-width` is a ceiling. The image keeps its natural size until the container is narrower, then it shrinks.

quiz.q: Make every element use the easier sizing model.
quiz.explain: `* { box-sizing: border-box; }` is a common first rule in real stylesheets.

exercise.task:
Size the `.panel` and the image placeholder. Work in `index.html`.

- `.panel`: `box-sizing: border-box`, `width: 300px`, `padding: 20px`, `height: 120px`.
- `.panel`: also `max-width: 100%` so it never overflows.
- `.photo`: `width: 100%` and `max-width: 400px`.
hints: Four properties for .panel and two for .photo. Declarations are separated by semicolons.
`box-sizing: border-box` makes the width include the padding. `max-width` is a limit, `width` is the target.

checks.name: .photo takes the width of its container, up to 400px
checks.hint: Add width: 100%; to .photo. In a wide frame the max-width caps it at 400px.
